text:
Why did Mata Hari refuse a blindfold and blow a kiss to her firing squad before execution?
A blindfold provides psychological comfort to the firing squad, not the victim. By refusing one, Mata Hari forced 12 executioners to look her in the eye for her final performance.

Her execution on October 15, 1917, remains one of the most mythologized events of World War I. Born Margaretha Zelle in the Netherlands, she had spent a decade convincing Parisian high society that she was a Javanese princess and an exotic temple dancer. Her entire public life was a masterclass in illusion and theatricality, and she approached her death with the same meticulous stagecraft.

At dawn, she arrived at the Château de Vincennes impeccably dressed. Eyewitness accounts from journalists, including Henry Wales of the International News Service, noted her pristine attire—a custom-made corset, a tailored dark coat, a tricorn hat, and gloves. She was not a broken woman begging for mercy, but a cosmopolitan celebrity facing an audience.

When an officer approached to tie her to the stake and offer a blindfold, she declined both. She reportedly asked if it was truly necessary that she be bound, and when permitted, stood mostly unrestrained. Refusing the blindfold served two main purposes.

First, it maintained her aura of fearlessness. Mata Hari had always projected an image of an untouchable femme fatale who lived on her own terms. A blindfold would have signaled submission or shame—traits completely at odds with the persona she had cultivated.

Second, it was a statement of a clear conscience. Though she admitted to accepting money from a German diplomat, she steadfastly denied ever handing over valuable military intelligence. She considered herself a woman of the world caught in a geopolitical game rather than a traitor. Hiding her eyes would have implied guilt; facing the rifles head-on signaled she had nothing to hide.

As the squad raised their rifles, legend holds she blew a kiss to the soldiers or to her lawyer, Édouard Clunet. Whether the kiss was a theatrical flourish or simply a polite farewell nod romanticized by the press, her refusal to hide her eyes is undisputed historical fact. It ensured she would be immortalized not as a weeping casualty of war, but as the ultimate fearless seductress.

🚨 BREAKING NEWS: FLORIDA UNDERWATER! MORE THAN TWO FEET OF RAIN TRIGGERS MASSIVE FLOOD EMERGENCY!

Hundreds of high-water rescues reported as torrential rainfall overwhelms communities along Florida's Space Coast.

🇺🇸 BREVARD COUNTY, FLORIDA | NOVEMBER 4, 2026
A devastating rainfall event has inundated portions of Florida's Atlantic coast, flooding neighborhoods, stranding motorists, forcing evacuations, and prompting a state of emergency across seven counties.

The hardest-hit communities include Palm Bay, Melbourne, Malabar, Grant-Valkaria, and Barefoot Bay, where relentless rainfall transformed streets into waterways and left residents struggling to protect their homes and belongings.

According to preliminary National Weather Service observations, an extraordinary 24.10 inches of rain fell near Malabar during the event that began November 1.

That is more than two feet of rainfall.

In some locations, the amount of water that fell over just a few days approached what would ordinarily accumulate over several months.

The resulting flooding overwhelmed drainage systems, submerged vehicles, and sent emergency responders into dangerous conditions.

🌧️ AN EXTREME RAINFALL DISASTER

The flooding developed as persistent tropical moisture and heavy thunderstorms repeatedly affected Florida's east-central coast.

Instead of passing quickly through the region, rain-producing storms continued affecting many of the same communities.

This allowed extraordinary rainfall totals to accumulate.

As the ground became saturated and drainage systems reached capacity, water began spreading into residential streets, businesses, and low-lying neighborhoods.

The National Weather Service reported preliminary rainfall totals exceeding 20 inches in some areas, with approximately 24.10 inches recorded near Malabar.

These measurements illustrate the exceptional nature of the event.

Even communities accustomed to Florida's tropical downpours can experience catastrophic flooding when rainfall accumulates this rapidly.

Roads become impassable.

Vehicles stall in rising water.

Homes experience water intrusion.

And emergency services face an enormous challenge reaching people trapped by the flooding.

🚨 MORE THAN 200 HIGH-WATER RESCUES

The Brevard County Sheriff's Office reported approximately 204 high-water rescues during the emergency.

That figure represents a major emergency-response operation involving residents and motorists caught in dangerous conditions.

Floodwater can conceal hazards that are difficult to recognize from the surface.

Roadways may be washed out beneath the water.

Vehicles can lose traction or become disabled.

Storm drains and drainage canals may create powerful currents.

And even relatively shallow moving water can sweep a person off their feet.

Emergency officials repeatedly urged motorists to avoid flooded roads rather than attempting to drive through them.

For rescue personnel, every flooded roadway creates another potential emergency.

Crews worked to reach stranded residents while monitoring conditions that could change rapidly.

🏠 NEIGHBORHOODS CUT OFF BY FLOODWATER

Communities across southern Brevard County experienced significant flooding.

Palm Bay and surrounding neighborhoods were among the areas facing dangerous conditions.

Some streets became inaccessible, leaving residents unable to travel safely.

Flooded vehicles and standing water created additional obstacles for emergency crews.

Local authorities issued warnings and coordinated assistance for residents in affected neighborhoods.

The extent of property damage was still being assessed as floodwaters began receding in some areas.

But the danger did not disappear when the heaviest rainfall ended.

Standing water can remain for days, particularly in low-lying neighborhoods where drainage is limited.

Floodwater may also contain sewage, fuel, chemicals, and other contaminants.

Residents returning to damaged properties face additional risks from electrical systems, structural damage, and contaminated materials.

⚠️ SEVEN COUNTIES UNDER EMERGENCY DECLARATION

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency covering seven counties in response to the flooding threat and its consequences.

The declaration was intended to support emergency coordination, resource deployment, and response efforts.

Such declarations can help state and local agencies mobilize personnel, equipment, and assistance where they are needed most.

However, an emergency declaration does not mean every location within the affected counties experienced catastrophic flooding.

The most severe conditions were concentrated in particular communities.

Officials continued assessing damage, monitoring water levels, and coordinating recovery operations.

🌊 WHY FLOODING CAN CONTINUE AFTER THE RAIN STOPS

One of the most dangerous aspects of extreme rainfall events is that the flooding can outlast the storm itself.

When enormous quantities of water accumulate, drainage canals, retention ponds, and natural waterways may remain elevated long after the clouds begin clearing.

Water can continue flowing into lower elevations.

Roads that appear passable may remain structurally unsafe.

And saturated soil can delay recovery efforts.

The National Weather Service warned that flood conditions could persist even after the heaviest rainfall moved away.

Residents were urged to continue following official warnings and avoid driving into standing water.

The familiar safety message remains critically important:

TURN AROUND, DON'T DROWN.

No destination is worth risking a life by entering an unknown depth of floodwater.

🇺🇸 A REMINDER OF AMERICA'S WEATHER VULNERABILITY

Florida is no stranger to hurricanes, tropical storms, and powerful thunderstorms.

But extreme flooding does not always require a named hurricane.

Persistent rainfall alone can produce a major disaster.

This event demonstrates how quickly normal daily life can be disrupted when drainage infrastructure is overwhelmed.

Homes, businesses, roads, and emergency services can all be affected simultaneously.

It also illustrates why weather preparedness matters even outside the most recognizable hurricane emergencies.

Families in flood-prone communities benefit from knowing evacuation routes, keeping essential medications and documents accessible, and monitoring official warnings.

The people of Brevard County now face the difficult process of cleanup, damage assessment, and recovery.

For some residents, that recovery could take considerably longer than the storm itself.

📖 BIBLE PERSPECTIVE — THE POWER OF THE STORM

The Bible repeatedly reminds us of the extraordinary power of nature and humanity's dependence upon God.

PSALM 107:28–29 (KJV)

"Then they cry unto the LORD in their trouble, and he bringeth them out of their distresses.

He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still."

Scripture also records Jesus demonstrating authority over the wind and the sea.

MARK 4:39 (KJV)

"And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm."

For Christians watching disasters unfold around the world, these passages offer a reminder that our ultimate security is found in the Lord.

Jesus also warned that the world would experience upheaval and distress.

LUKE 21:11 (KJV)

"And great earthquakes shall be in divers places, and famines, and pestilences; and fearful sights and great signs shall there be from heaven."

That verse does not specifically predict this Florida flood.

We should not claim that every natural disaster fulfills an individual prophecy or represents divine punishment against its victims.

But such events remind us of the fragility of human life and the importance of remaining spiritually prepared.

We should pray for those affected, support relief efforts, and help neighbors whenever possible.

Faith and practical preparedness belong together.

🚨 THE BOTTOM LINE

Florida's Space Coast has experienced an extraordinary flooding disaster.

Preliminary rainfall observations reached approximately 24.10 inches near Malabar.

The Brevard County Sheriff's Office reported 204 high-water rescues.

Seven counties were included in a state emergency declaration.

Communities including Palm Bay, Melbourne, Malabar, Grant-Valkaria, and Barefoot Bay experienced significant flooding.

Although the heaviest rainfall has eased, lingering floodwater and the recovery process remain serious concerns.

MORE THAN TWO FEET OF RAIN. HUNDREDS OF RESCUES. ENTIRE NEIGHBORHOODS DISRUPTED.

For the families affected, this is not simply another weather headline.

It is a disaster that has changed their lives.

Pray for Florida's flood victims, emergency responders, and families facing the difficult days ahead.

STAY FAITHFUL. STAY PREPARED. STAY ON COURSE.

ISRAEL RETURNED HIS SON AS A BLOCK OF ICE. FATHER FEARED THEY HAD PUT HIM IN A BODY BAG WHILE STILL ALIVE

On 12 October 2015, Israeli police shot dead 15-year-old Hassan Manasra in East Jerusalem.

Hassan and his 13-year-old cousin Ahmad had attacked Israeli civilians with knives, seriously wounding two people, including a 13-year-old boy.

These were morally wrong acts, committed in the context of decades of brutal treatment of Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank. When force is used to systematically oppress a people, some will respond with indiscriminate violence themselves. Injustice then becomes entrenched, with resistance to injustice used as a rationale for further oppression. 

According to Israeli police, Hassan and Ahmad were motivated by anger over Israel’s treatment of Palestinians and perceived threats to Al-Aqsa Mosque. 

What makes the case extra grim is how Israeli authorities compounded the family's suffering through their treatment of Hassan's body in a most morbid way.

Israeli authorities kept Hassan's body for months.

When they finally offered to return him, his body was frozen solid. His family could not bear to bury him like that. They refused to accept the remains, and Israeli authorities took them away again.

The conditions imposed by Israeli authorities included a 20,000-shekel deposit, immediate burial and a maximum of 30 mourners.

Only seven months after Hassan's death was his family finally able to bury him.

His father, Khaled, later described seeing what he believed were frozen tears on his son's face. His mouth was partly open, with dried blood around it.

He desperately wondered whether Hassan might still have been alive, crying out for help, when his body was sealed inside the black bag. Whether his son had suffocated there, or inside the freezer.

Palestinian scholar Nadera Shalhoub-Kevorkian documented his testimony.

Think about what it means to lose your child. Then imagine being denied his body for months, having to negotiate the conditions under which you may bury him, and finally receiving him frozen.

"All I'm asking for is the right to bury my son in peace, without restrictions," Khaled told Al Jazeera in April 2016.

Hassan had participated in a terrible attack. Hard to fathom what motivaged him that day. His Israeli victims deserved justice.

But what does a state hope to accomplish when it uses the body of a dead child as a sordid way to keep his family, who were not involved in his crime, from mourning and burying their son in peace?

---

SOURCES AND FURTHER READING

Nadera Shalhoub-Kevorkian, Incarcerated Childhood and the Politics of Unchilding (Cambridge University Press, 2019). Hassan Manasra's case and his father's testimony appear on pages 96–97, particularly page 97.

Nadera Shalhoub-Kevorkian, “Persistent Faces: Palestinian Fatherhood against Necropower” (2023). The father's account of the frozen tears, partly open mouth and fear that Hassan had still been alive appears on page 82.

https://t.co/TaCp6jTCGm

YouTube interview with Nadera Shalhoub-Kevorkian, in which she recounts the father's testimony.

https://t.co/oJZ3XfiqTU

https://t.co/Zmz854bhrQ

https://t.co/UqNtwifcA9

text:
CHARGEPOINT $CHPT POSTS ITS HIGHEST CLOSE IN A YEAR:

ChargePoint (CHPT) at $10.79, +$0.91 / +9.21% on Tuesday, and $10.91 premarket, +$0.12 / +1.11% from that close.

ChargePoint is #7 on the Momentum Len5 and fits none of the other styles we weigh, because the Campbell, California maker of the chargers in office lots and fleet depots, and of the software that runs them, still loses money and owes more than it owns. Tuesday's close is its highest since October 31, 2025, on no news from the company, a day after LS Power bid to take rival EVgo private and as clean-energy buyers bet on the midterm count. The run rests on one quarter that beat the company's own forecast, and the forecast for the quarter it reports in December is lower.

- Momentum Len5: a strong fit. Momentum wants months of gains with the shares near their high, and ChargePoint has more than doubled since its September 2 report, with Tuesday's close 4.2% under the October 2 high of $11.26. What would knock it off the Momentum Len5: an October quarter under the $105 million to $115 million ChargePoint forecast, which would hand back the September gap.
- Quality-Value Len5: not a fit. Quality-Value wants a durable business at a price its own profit justifies, and ChargePoint lost $35.6 million in the July quarter, so there is no profit to price. A year of profit under standard accounting would be the first step onto the Quality-Value Len5.
- Deep-Value and Special-Situations Len5: not a fit. That Len5 wants a business priced under a cautious value of what it earns, or an event an owner can count on, and the only event is next door, at EVgo. A signed offer for ChargePoint itself would put it on the Deep-Value and Special-Situations Len5.
- Hypergrowth Len5: not a fit. Hypergrowth wants sales multiplying at a company that already earns a profit; ChargePoint's revenue grew 18% in the July quarter and the loss continued. Charging-system sales doubling on the Express Solo fast charger, which reaches full production this winter, would put it on the Hypergrowth Len5.
- Income Len5: not a fit. Income wants cash paid to owners that the business covers, and ChargePoint pays no dividend, with $95 million of cash against $237 million of debt; a dividend needs a profit ahead of it.
- Quality Len5: not a fit, on the same books. ChargePoint owed $732 million against $696 million of assets at July 31, so the owners' stake is $36 million below zero.

The quarter the run is built on, reported September 2 for the three months ended July 31:
- Revenue $116.1M, +18%, above the $100M to $110M ChargePoint had forecast; charging-system sales $62.9M, +25%; subscriptions $43.7M, +10%.
- Net loss $35.6M from $66.2M; gross margin, what it keeps of each sales dollar after building the chargers, 36% from 31%, 4 points of it a one-time tariff refund.
The shares rose 75% the next day. Mansi Khetani, ChargePoint's chief financial officer, said the beat came from home-charger sales around big online sale days and "we don't expect that bump to happen again in Q3," so the October-quarter forecast is about 4% growth at the midpoint.

EVgo (EVGO) at $1.83, -$0.02 / -1.08% on Tuesday, owns and runs its own fast-charging stations, where ChargePoint sells the chargers to whoever owns the site. On Monday LS Power, the privately held power investor that holds about 56% of EVgo's votes, proposed $2.00 a share in cash for the shares it does not own, 59% above Friday's close; EVgo rose 47% that day, its board formed a special committee, and the proposal binds no one. EVgo is on none of the Momentum, Quality-Value, Deep-Value and Special-Situations, Hypergrowth or Income Len5es: a non-binding offer from its own controlling owner is not an event the Deep-Value and Special-Situations Len5 can count on.

Tuesday's 9% gain came as options traders bought clean-energy calls ahead of the midterm count; options volume in the Invesco Solar ETF (TAN), at $43.34, +$1.27 / +3.02% on Tuesday, ran about 40 times normal, 99% of it calls. Our read: the bet on a Congress friendlier to electric vehicles reached the charging names, and the Associated Press called both chambers for Democrats overnight.

ChargePoint reports the October quarter tentatively on December 3 after the close; analysts expect a loss of about $0.61 a share. Revenue inside the $105 million to $115 million forecast keeps the run a Momentum story; a quarter under it makes the $237 million of debt the story.

Not investment advice.

text:
IN DEPTH | The Trump era draws to a close as American voters abandon the president who promised to put them first

WASHINGTON – For more than a decade, Donald Trump has dominated American politics, building a movement around his personality, defying political convention, and cultivating a loyal following that appeared impervious to controversy. But the 2026 midterm elections have exposed a profound fracture in that political empire, with voters turning against the very presidency they once entrusted with reshaping America.

The Democrats' sweeping congressional victories have redrawn the political landscape, delivering a verdict on a presidency increasingly defined by the distance between its promises and the realities confronting ordinary Americans.

Trump had made the elections a personal test of his leadership, repeatedly urging voters to imagine that he was on the ballot. They took him at his word. The result was a decisive rejection of his Republican candidates and the policies underpinning his second administration.

The disillusionment was rooted in mounting economic pressures, with persistently high fuel prices and tariffs adding to the cost of living for American households. A president who campaigned on economic relief and an end to foreign wars instead found himself presiding over an increasingly intractable conflict with Iran, while his aggressive immigration crackdown generated resistance among voters concerned about the treatment of long-established immigrant communities.

Allegations of profiteering involving Trump and members of his inner circle further eroded confidence in an administration that had promised to dismantle the political establishment and put ordinary Americans first.

Even Republican strongholds offered no refuge. The defeat of Trump's preferred candidates in Texas and South Carolina exposed the diminishing reach of his political endorsement, while his efforts to reshape congressional districts to secure Republican dominance failed to deliver the electoral protection he had sought.

The consequences reach far beyond the ballot box. Democratic control of Congress threatens to obstruct Trump's legislative ambitions, intensify the scrutiny of his administration, and fundamentally alter the balance of power in Washington.

For a president who has spent years demanding personal loyalty and presenting himself as the indispensable force in American conservatism, the results expose the fragility of a movement built so heavily around one man.

Trump remains in the White House, but the political architecture that sustained his dominance has suffered a major fracture. The voters who once embraced his promise of disruption have now turned against the consequences of his rule.

The midterms have not ended Trump's presidency, but they may have ended the political era in which his influence appeared beyond challenge.

Reporting by Anesu Masamvu

text:
US Midterms 2026: Congressional Power Rebalancing and Global Strategic Consequences - The November 3, 2026 midterm elections have produced a substantial change in the prospective balance of power in Washington. Election-night reporting indicates Democratic control of the House of Representatives and Senate, although final certified seat totals and the resulting congressional committee arrangements remain outstanding. The decisive institutional consequence is not the disappearance of presidential authority but its redistribution across legislative, financial, investigative and executive channels.

The outgoing Senate contains 53 Republicans, 45 Democrats and two independents caucusing with Democrats, giving Republicans a 53–47 organizational advantage. The electoral reversal, including reported Democratic Senate gains in traditionally Republican states, is geographically broader than a narrow redistribution of competitive suburban constituencies. However, electoral breadth alone cannot establish a durable partisan realignment.

The new congressional majority will acquire substantial influence over appropriations, committee oversight, investigations, legislative scheduling and Senate confirmations when the 120th Congress convenes on January 3, 2027. It will not automatically acquire the power to enact its own programme against presidential opposition. The two-thirds veto-override requirement and the Senate’s ordinary 60-vote legislative cloture threshold remain fundamental constraints.

The presidency retains constitutional command authority, diplomatic initiative, enforcement discretion and substantial statutory powers over sanctions, trade administration and executive implementation. Those powers remain subject to legislation, judicial review, appropriations and specific statutory limitations.

For foreign governments, the principal consequence is a more complex American decision-making structure. Congressional support for an international commitment may coexist with executive resistance; conversely, presidential diplomatic or military initiatives may encounter congressional opposition without necessarily being stopped immediately.

Principal judgment — High confidence: The 2027–2028 period will be characterized by stronger congressional constraints on new domestic legislation and appointments, but potentially continuing executive initiative in diplomacy, sanctions and foreign-policy implementation.

Decisive uncertainty — Medium confidence: The extent to which the new majorities translate electoral gains into coordinated policy decisions, rather than investigations, budgetary confrontation and selective legislative compromises.

America’s Divided Government: The Cost of Political Fragmentation for Global Security
The November 3, 2026 US midterm elections have created a contradiction with consequences far beyond Washington: a presidency retaining substantial control over foreign policy and military operations now faces a reported Democratic majority in both chambers of Congress, capable of constraining legislation, appropriations and senior appointments. The reversal comes as the United States records a $1.992 trillion federal deficit, Europe finances a €90 billion Ukraine support programme, and the conflict involving Iran disrupts global petroleum supplies. These pressures will not disappear with a change in congressional leadership. Nor will presidential authority. The governing question for 2027–2028 is whether American institutions can translate competing political mandates into legally financed and operationally executable commitments. The principal international risk is not divided government itself, but the widening gap between Washington’s capacity to announce policy and its capacity to sustain it.

The Electoral Reversal Changes Congress, Not the Presidency
The November 2026 elections reportedly transferred control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate to the Democratic Party, with Senate gains in seven previously Republican-held states: Texas, Kansas, Iowa, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina. The geographic distribution extends beyond traditionally competitive constituencies, although final certified margins remain outstanding. The outgoing Senate contained 53 Republicans, 45 Democrats and two independents caucusing with Democrats, making the reported reversal consequential for legislative control, committee organization and confirmation procedures.

The institutional transition begins on January 3, 2027, when the 120th Congress assumes office under the Twentieth Amendment. President Donald Trump’s second term continues until January 20, 2029. Democratic congressional control therefore creates divided government without transferring the president’s executive authority. The new majorities can determine committee leadership, expand investigations, influence appropriations and control Senate confirmation proceedings, but cannot independently implement a legislative programme against presidential opposition.

The constitutional arithmetic explains the constraint. Most contested Senate legislation remains subject to a cloture threshold normally requiring 60 votes, while overriding a presidential veto requires two-thirds of those voting in each chamber, provided a quorum is present. If all members participate, that corresponds to 67 senators and 290 representatives. Formal treaty ratification separately requires the consent of two-thirds of senators present. These requirements make congressional control a powerful instrument for blocking or negotiating legislation, but not an automatic mechanism for replacing executive policy.

Historical precedents offer limited reassurance. The opposition party gained 54 House seats in 1994, 32 in 2006, 64 in 2010 and 41 in 2018. Those transitions produced different combinations of legislative confrontation, oversight and executive initiative. The reported 2026 change is institutionally distinct from 2018 because Democratic control extends to both chambers. It remains insufficient, however, to demonstrate permanent electoral realignment or establish the outcome of the 2028 presidential election.

A $1.992 Trillion Deficit Restricts the Fiscal Choices Available to Both Parties
The fiscal arithmetic places an immediate ceiling on competing political programmes. In fiscal year 2026, federal net outlays reached $7.396 trillion, against receipts of $5.403 trillion, producing a deficit of approximately $1.992 trillion, compared with $1.775 trillion in fiscal year 2025. The deficit increased by approximately $217 billion, or 12.2%, while annual receipts financed roughly 73.1% of expenditure. For every dollar collected, Washington spent approximately $1.37.

These figures describe annual budgetary flows, not the outstanding stock of federal debt. The Congressional Budget Office’s February 2026 baseline had projected public debt of approximately $32.1 trillion at the fiscal year’s conclusion, illustrating the scale of financing requirements already anticipated before the election. Divided government inherits these obligations; it does not dissolve them.

A Democratic Congress can influence spending legislation and taxation, while the president retains veto authority and responsibility for lawful budget execution. Neither institution can impose a comprehensive fiscal settlement without satisfying the applicable legislative requirements. The result is a structural incentive toward negotiated appropriations, limited statutory adjustments and disputes over the allocation of resources rather than an immediate reconstruction of the federal budget.

The executive’s capacity to withhold enacted funding is also legally constrained. On September 29, 2026, the Government Accountability Office examined presidential rescission proposals affecting eleven appropriation accounts and concluded that the proposed rescissions did not authorize withholding the relevant funds beyond the fiscal year’s end without congressional enactment. The Impoundment Control Act of 1974 thus remains a consequential boundary between presidential budget preferences and congressional spending authority.

For international partners, the distinction is practical: an American assistance announcement is not an appropriation, an appropriation is not a financial obligation, and an obligation is not proof of delivery. Defence manufacturers, infrastructure investors and foreign governments must distinguish each stage before treating federal commitments as available resources.

The Trade Conflict Has Moved From Emergency Powers to Statutory Competition
The American trade system entered the elections after a major judicial restriction on presidential tariff authority. On February 20, 2026, the Supreme Court ruled that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act did not authorize the tariffs imposed under the emergency powers examined in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump and Trump v. V.O.S. Selections, Inc. The decision restricted one legal instrument without eliminating the executive’s ability to impose trade measures under other statutes.

The administration subsequently employed Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 to impose a temporary 10% global tariff, which expired on July 24, 2026. Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 and Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 remained relevant instruments for national-security-related import restrictions and responses to specified foreign trade practices, subject to their respective statutory requirements.

This legal structure creates an asymmetric form of economic power. Congress can amend trade legislation and scrutinize administrative findings, but the executive retains operational flexibility where valid statutory delegations already exist. The disappearance of unified party control therefore does not guarantee tariff stability or a general reduction in trade restrictions.

The distinction is particularly important for industrial investment. Semiconductor facilities, advanced manufacturing plants, defence production lines and energy infrastructure require commitments extending well beyond a congressional term. Changes in trade regulations, export licences or procurement conditions can affect capital allocation before legislators negotiate comprehensive reforms.

The January 13, 2026 decision by the Bureau of Industry and Security to revise licensing treatment for certain advanced semiconductors exported to China illustrates the mechanism. Products including the NVIDIA H200 and AMD MI325X became subject to individual licensing review under specified security conditions. Such decisions can alter commercial access and technology supply chains through administrative implementation, even when Congress remains divided over broader economic legislation.

Sanctions follow a different legal structure. The Supreme Court’s restriction on emergency tariff authority did not generally invalidate non-tariff sanctions under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. Congressional statutes, executive designations, licensing decisions and enforcement procedures continue to determine the actual operation of restrictions affecting Russia, Iran and other jurisdictions. Legal continuity and administrative discretion therefore matter more than a generalized assumption that congressional opposition neutralizes economic statecraft.

Europe Has €90 Billion for Ukraine but Cannot Finance Its Way Out of Every Dependency
The European Union enters the new American congressional period with a more substantial financing architecture for Ukraine. On April 23, 2026, the Council finalized a €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan for 2026–2027, comprising an indicative €30 billion for macroeconomic support and €60 billion for defence and industrial requirements. An initial €45 billion was made accessible for 2026, including €8.35 billion in macro-financial assistance, €8.35 billion through the Ukraine Facility and €28.3 billion for defence-industrial capacity.

These amounts represent components of the same financing framework, not separate commitments that can be added to the €90 billion total. Their significance lies in separating the financial survival of the Ukrainian state from the procurement and production of military capabilities. European borrowing can support both functions, but it cannot automatically manufacture missiles, ammunition or air-defence systems.

The financing requirement extends beyond the immediate instrument. The European Council identified approximately €30 billion in additional international financing needs in March 2026, while the International Monetary Fund assessed Ukraine’s cumulative 2026–2029 financing gap at approximately $140.3 billion under its baseline scenario, including $55.4 billion in 2026 and $43.4 billion in 2027. These figures use different definitions and must not be added mechanically.

Russian sovereign assets provide a further example of the distinction between financial stocks and available resources. Approximately €210 billion in Russian central-bank assets remained immobilized within the European Union according to the Council’s October 14, 2026 review. Extraordinary revenues generated approximately €8 billion, of which €3.8 billion had reached Ukraine and €4.2 billion had supported or been reserved for repayment mechanisms. The underlying €210 billion stock is not equivalent to money transferred to Kyiv.

NATO’s June 25, 2025 Hague Summit Declaration adds a longer-term financial obligation: allied investment equivalent to 5% of GDP by 2035, consisting of at least 3.5% for core defence requirements and up to 1.5% for broader defence- and security-related activities. The European Union’s separate SAFE instrument provides up to €150 billion in eligible defence loans. Neither the NATO commitment nor SAFE represents military equipment already delivered.

European exposure remains differentiated. Germany must translate expenditure into industrial production and continental readiness. France combines national military autonomy with European defence-industrial coordination. The United Kingdom retains bilateral American security relationships while participating in eligible European Ukraine procurement arrangements following the Council’s July 22, 2026 approval. Italy faces the combined constraints of Mediterranean security, manufacturing exposure, fiscal capacity and defence-supply-chain qualification.

The consequence is that European financial autonomy has advanced faster than the ability to demonstrate independence across every critical military capability. American congressional rebalancing may improve or complicate particular assistance channels, but Europe’s underlying production, logistics and procurement constraints remain its own responsibility.

Iran Has Turned American Crisis Management Into a Global Energy Cost
The United States and Israel initiated military operations against Iran on February 28, 2026, creating an ongoing controversy concerning presidential command authority, congressional authorization and the War Powers Resolution. The November election changes the political environment surrounding those operations without automatically terminating them. The president retains command authority subject to constitutional and statutory limits, while Congress can exercise oversight and enact legally effective financial or operational restrictions through the required legislative procedures.

The economic consequences extend well beyond the legal dispute in Washington. The International Energy Agency’s October 14, 2026 report recorded world oil supply of 102.3 million barrels per day in September, following a monthly recovery of 2.5 million barrels per day. Nevertheless, the agency projected average global supply of only 100.7 million barrels per day for 2026, representing a year-on-year reduction of 5.8 million barrels per day.

The disruption is particularly severe in refined products. Gulf crude exports recovered to approximately 13.9 million barrels per day in September, while flows through the Strait of Hormuz reached 10.9 million barrels per day. Yet Middle Eastern refined-product exports stood at only 1.9 million barrels per day, compared with 4.7 million before the war. Liquefied petroleum gas exports recovered to approximately 670,000 barrels per day, against a pre-war level of 1.5 million. Global observed inventories declined by 509 million barrels between the end of February and the end of September.

These figures explain why improved crude shipments do not establish energy-market normalization. Refineries, shipping routes, insurance, pipelines and export terminals remain separate potential bottlenecks. The September attack on Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline demonstrated that bypass infrastructure can reduce dependence on the Strait of Hormuz without eliminating vulnerability to regional attacks.

For Italy, Germany, France and the United Kingdom, the transmission occurs through industrial energy costs, freight, aviation fuel, shipping insurance and purchasing power. For Asian importing economies, the availability of crude grades and refined products creates additional exposure. Congressional opposition in Washington may alter the political sustainability of prolonged operations, but it cannot by itself restore damaged infrastructure or remove physical maritime risks.

The Indo-Pacific Tests Whether Deterrence Can Survive Administrative Uncertainty
American commitments in the Indo-Pacific depend on several legal and operational arrangements that cannot be treated as interchangeable. Japan, the Republic of Korea and the Philippines have distinct treaty-based security relationships with Washington, while Taiwan’s position is governed by a different domestic statutory and diplomatic framework. The credibility of these commitments depends not only on presidential statements but also on force readiness, logistics, procurement, technology controls and the resources required for implementation.

Congressional appropriations can affect defence production and security assistance, while executive agencies retain powers over military deployment and export licensing under applicable law. This creates the possibility that diplomatic assurances continue while particular procurement programmes experience funding or production delays. Equally, targeted bipartisan agreements could preserve technology-security and defence-industrial programmes despite confrontation elsewhere in Washington.

The semiconductor licensing decision of January 13, 2026 illustrates the significance of administrative authority in strategic competition with China. Product-specific licensing can change access to advanced computing technologies without the adoption of a comprehensive new industrial statute. The resulting effects extend through semiconductor manufacturers, suppliers, investors and allied technology industries, making regulatory predictability an operational component of economic security.

The Indo-Pacific therefore exposes a longer-duration version of the problem visible in Ukraine: a political commitment can remain intact while the resources necessary to execute it become subject to separate institutional decisions. For allied governments, the critical evidence lies in signed agreements, appropriations, export-control rules, procurement contracts and delivered capabilities rather than declarations of strategic intent.

The Next 24 Months Will Price the Difference Between Commitment and Delivery
Three institutional pathways remain possible through 2028. Legislative gridlock could coexist with continued presidential action through existing foreign-policy, trade and sanctions authorities. Selective bipartisan agreements could preserve particular procurement, technology and assistance programmes without producing wider political consensus. Intensified confrontation could generate funding disputes, confirmation delays, litigation and interruptions in implementation. These mechanisms may operate simultaneously across different policy sectors; none can be assigned a defensible numerical probability from the election result alone.

The relevant indicators are legally consequential. Enacted appropriations matter more than funding proposals; confirmed appointments matter more than nomination announcements; operative judicial orders matter more than the filing of lawsuits; and completed defence deliveries matter more than declared procurement values. The Government Accountability Office’s September 2026 decision on rescissions demonstrates that conflicts over public expenditure can have concrete statutory limits, while the constitutional veto and Senate procedures constrain the ability of either congressional majority or presidency to impose new legislation independently.

Over the next 12–24 months, the direct costs of unresolved institutional confrontation will fall on programmes requiring new financing, industries exposed to changes in tariffs and export controls, and foreign partners dependent on American procurement or security assistance. European taxpayers may face additional financing pressures where national or EU institutions choose to compensate for delayed support. Defence contractors and their suppliers may absorb production uncertainty. Energy-importing businesses and households remain exposed to Gulf disruptions regardless of Washington’s internal legislative balance.

The central fiscal contradiction is already measurable: $7.396 trillion in annual federal expenditure against $5.403 trillion in receipts, alongside international commitments requiring financing and industrial execution across multiple years. The November 2026 elections redistribute political authority but do not reduce these obligations.

The cost of inaction will therefore be borne less by the institutions announcing competing policies than by the governments, manufacturers, investors and households required to operate under the resulting uncertainty. Between January 2027 and the end of 2028, American international credibility will be measured increasingly by the legal durability, financial provision and operational delivery of its commitments—not by the political authority claimed to support them.

They turned their backyard swimming pool into a $100,000 side hustle. 🏊💰

Crail and Joey from Austin, Texas, had a swimming pool they mostly used themselves.

During the pandemic, they started letting neighbors book it using a shared Google Calendar.

Then they discovered Swimply — a platform that lets people rent private swimming pools by the hour.

They listed their backyard.

The next morning, they already had five bookings.

Here's how the business works:

1. Take professional photos of your pool and backyard.
2. Create a listing on Swimply.
3. Set your hourly rate and minimum booking time.
4. Offer extras like lounge chairs, heating, towels, and outdoor entertainment.
5. Let customers book private swimming sessions or parties.

Their reported numbers:

- More than $100,000 in cumulative earnings.
- Nearly $30,000 in their best year.
- Around 96 bookings during their busiest season.

They also reinvested some of the money into a pool heater, cabanas, and better outdoor furniture.

Important: that's reported income before accounting for all maintenance and operating costs. A swimming pool isn't exactly free to run.

But here's the interesting business idea:

People aren't necessarily looking for a hotel or a water park. Sometimes they just want a private pool for a birthday party, a family afternoon, or a few hours of relaxation.

If you owned a swimming pool, would you share it with strangers for $100 an hour?

text:
THE WORLD HAS JUST BEEN REMINDED OF SOMETHING: PEOPLE CAN CHANGE THEIR MINDS. YOUR CUSTOMERS CAN TOO.

Look at the elections taking place around the world. Beyond the political drama, there are lessons every entrepreneur, freelancer, content creator and business owner should pay attention to.

Consider Brazil.

Lula da Silva secured re-election on October 25 with 51.79% of the vote against Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.21%. That's a reminder that even a closely contested race can turn on how people respond to competing messages and choices.

Then look at Texas, where James Talarico defeated Ken Paxton in a Senate race, securing a Democratic Senate victory in the state for the first time since 1988. His campaign's message focused on the economic divide between wealthy people and everyone else. 

And Serbia's October election showed that participation and public trust matter too. International observers reported high turnout but also concerns about unequal campaign conditions and pressure on voters. 

Now, forget politics for a moment. Let's talk business.

**HERE ARE FIVE LESSONS WORTH STEALING FROM THE ELECTION SEASON.**

1. A familiar name doesn't guarantee loyalty.

Your customers may have bought from you for years. That doesn't mean they'll stay if someone else offers better value.

Never confuse familiarity with loyalty.

2. Your message must address people's real concerns.

You can spend months telling people how excellent your product is.

But if customers are worried about price, convenience, quality or reliability, that's what they want you to address.

Stop advertising what you love about your business. Start communicating what matters to your customers.

3. Visibility is not the same as influence.

Having 50,000 followers doesn't mean 50,000 people trust you.

A smaller audience that believes in your work can be more valuable than a massive audience that scrolls past everything you publish.

4. Never underestimate the competition.

The competitor you're ignoring may be studying your weaknesses while you're busy celebrating your market position.

Keep improving.

5. Don't disappear after winning.

Winning customers is one thing. Keeping them is another.

Deliver what you promised. Communicate. Solve problems. Build trust.

Your business doesn't get a permanent mandate simply because someone bought from you once.

THE BIG LESSON?

Whether you're selling a service, pitching a client, applying for a contract or building an audience, remember this:

People have choices.

Your job isn't to force them to choose you. It's to give them a compelling reason to.

Now, here's a question:

Are you building a business people genuinely want to choose, or are you simply hoping they'll keep choosing you because you've been around for a long time?

text:
Democrat Gina Hinojosa has unseated Gov. Greg Abbott, as Democrats won both the Texas governorship and a US Senate seat for the first time in decades.

CNN and NBC News projected Hinojosa the winner, denying Abbott a fourth term, and Abbott has conceded. The Austin state representative will be the first Democratic governor since Ann Richards left office in 1995, and the state's first Latina governor.

The result overturns the late polls, which had Abbott regaining the edge, and Cook Political Report's Lean R rating.

In the Senate race, James Talarico defeated Ken Paxton, the AP and NBC News project. He is the first Democrat to win a Texas Senate race since 1988. Outgoing Sen. John Cornyn congratulated him and offered help with the transition.

Democrats also held redistricted House seats in South Texas. Katy Padilla Stout flipped the 23rd district, while Vicente Gonzalez, Henry Cuellar and Johnny Garcia held the 34th, 28th and 35th.

Trump blamed Abbott for the loss, calling him a "RINO" who had become lax over the last six months of his term.

text:
In 2019, 19-year-old Cynthia Hoffman from Anchorage, Alaska, was mu*dered by someone she considered her best friend—all for a $9 million promise that never existed.

Cynthia’s body was found in the Eklutna River.

The person behind the horrifying crime was Denali Brehmer, who had been communicating online with a man calling himself “Tyler.” He claimed to be a millionaire from Kansas and offered Brehmer $9 million to mu*der someone in Alaska and send him Snapchat videos as proof.

Brehmer, then 18, chose Cynthia.

Cynthia had a developmental disability and was described as having the mental capacity of a 12-year-old. She trusted Brehmer and believed she was her best friend.

On June 2, 2019, Brehmer lured Cynthia to Thunderbird Falls.

There, 16-year-old Kayden McIntosh bound Cynthia with duct tape and shot her in the back of the head. Brehmer filmed the k*lling on Snapchat in real time.

Cynthia’s body was then dumped into the Eklutna River.

As her father, Timothy Hoffman, desperately searched through the night, Brehmer sent him a message:

“I hope she comes home safely. She’s my best friend.”

The words were a cruel deception.

On June 4, police knocked on Timothy’s door and delivered the devastating news: Cynthia was dead.

The man calling himself “Tyler” was actually Darin Schilmiller, a catfish from Indiana.

The promised $9 million never existed.

McIntosh reportedly believed he would receive $750,000. Instead, he was sentenced to 70 years in prison.

Brehmer was sentenced to 99 years.

But the tragedy did not end there.

In 2024, Cynthia’s father, Timothy, died in a motorcycle crash while participating in a memorial ride for his daughter.

A father who had spent the night searching for his missing child ultimately lost his life years later while honoring her memory.

Cynthia trusted someone she believed was her best friend—and that trust was tragically betrayed.

A fake identity. A nonexistent fortune. A young woman’s life stolen for a promise that was never real.

Cynthia Hoffman deserved friendship, protection and a future. She deserved so much more.

text:
Miracle in the Sunflower State: How Pastor Adam Hamilton flipped Kansas blue for the first time in 94 years.

For nearly a century, political conventional wisdom held that the Sunflower State was locked tight in Republican hands. Yet when election night settled, Kansas made history by electing Pastor Adam Hamilton to the U.S. Senate. Hamilton, the founding pastor of the nation's largest United Methodist congregation, pulled off the Democrats' first Senate victory in the state since 1932 by bridging deep political divides in the heart of America’s Bible Belt.

The turning point emerged in rural town halls where party loyalty clashed with everyday financial strain. Farmers, long the bedrock of Kansas conservative politics, found themselves squeezed by escalating trade conflicts. Retaliatory tariffs battered crop prices and closed international markets, leaving multi-generational agricultural operations struggling to stay afloat amidst mounting equipment and fertilizer expenses.

Compounding the pressure on family budgets was a surge in energy costs. Pain at the pump resonated deeply across vast rural counties where driving dozens of miles for basic groceries is standard. High gas prices directly inflated transport costs for local businesses and hit commuter families hard, turning kitchen-table economics into the dominant issue on the ballot.

Rather than relying on partisan rhetoric, Hamilton offered a moderate, faith-grounded message centered on practical solutions and economic relief. By connecting with voters on everyday pocketbook concerns— from lower fuel costs to tariff relief —he forged a unique coalition of suburbanites, independents, and disenchanted rural voters to claim a landmark victory over incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall.

Last night the Democrats took both the House and the Senate in a blue wave that reached into deep-red states. They did it the old way: by selling socialism with a smile.

Republicans assumed that after the body count of the 20th century, tens of millions dead under Stalin, Mao, Pol Pot, and the rest, and the living proof still on display in Venezuela, Cuba, and North Korea, Americans would never fall for the same package again. 

Free college, free healthcare, “equity,” green mandates, open borders, and government as the solution to every problem. 

History already ran the experiment. The results are mass graves, empty shelves, and broken economies.

Yet large numbers of voters bought it anyway. Schools and universities spent decades teaching that capitalism is the villain and that every failure is the fault of “the system.” 

Social media and legacy media amplified the pitch while memory-holing the body count. 

Younger voters especially have no lived memory of the Berlin Wall or the Soviet collapse; many were taught that the real threat is “far-right” skepticism of the state. Promises of redistribution and “fairness” sounded better than the hard reality of high prices, tariffs, and the costs of the Iran war. Economic frustration was real. 

Democrats offered the same old cure: more government, more spending, more control, dressed up as compassion.

Republicans did not fight hard enough. Too many treated the election as a referendum on personality or inflation alone instead of a clear fight over first principles. 

They soft-pedaled the socialist label on Democratic candidates, underplayed the long-term consequences of the policies being sold, and failed to make the historical case in plain language every voter could hear. Turnout and messaging gaps in places that should have been safe showed the cost. 

When the other side is offering free stuff paid for by someone else, and your side spends more time on process than on the stakes, a lot of people take the free stuff.

Communism and socialism do not become safer because the branding is softer or the salesmen wear suits. The record is the same: concentrated power, scarcity, and the erosion of individual liberty. 

The results last night show that a decisive number of Americans still do not believe that record, or have never been told it plainly. That is the fight that remains.

If more Republicans took off the gloves and fought harder like President Trump maybe this would not have happened. 

Now we have two years to prepare a strong Presidential candidate and take back our Country for good.

text:
Anakin is a great character who encompasses a very core and often misunderstood spiritual concept - avatarization.

The truth is that Anakin, even at the point of being denied the title of master, would have stood far higher in advancement in the spiritual realms than the whole of the council denying him.

Not from a standpoint of present-moment mastery but from the standpoint of sheer psychic and world-changing spiritual potential. This idea is reverberated throughout the whole narrative, over and over.

The concept of being chosen by unseen forces implies a natural predisposition to become avatarised and used by those higher forces - which he regularly is in order to avert disaster, especially when the council remains stagnant and, in many ways, incapable of taking decisive action.

The chosen one is simply he who is the most accurate embodiment of the grandest potential of creation, often to a point where it is to the detriment of their own mastery and advancement.

It is a very Promethean thing in attitude and theme.

The council remains the higher moral ground, yes, but the only reason they can even hold that sort of moral dominion over the other is because it is exactly the "foolishness" of the other that keeps them operational in the first place, even literally at times.

This implies that, as a character, Anakin has to remain flawed and unique in his temperaments in order for him to be used to his maximum effect by the unseen hand of destiny and divinity, even to the dislike of those who claim to listen and understand divine guidance.

He is not, like the others, simply listening to the spiritual forces shaping the world, he is quite literally inadvertently (because of his incredible natural aptitude) being actively used as a restorer of balance by those forces directly.

Many great historical figures in real world history embody this archetype as well, yet most of them make the same mistake Anakin does in his story - and that mistake seems close to impossible to not make once you understand what lies on the other side of it.

Because the other side of that incredible potential of the chosen avatar is a life of namelessness, of being unknown, doing good works from behind the curtain, so to speak.

It is the demand of ultimate humbleness from the universe contrasted by a strong inner knowing that you hold the greatest potential among your peers, the ambition and the desire to enact personal will over the world that stems from this is an incredible test to finalize a soul's mastery.

As a personal experiencer of this effect, it is, at times, near-impossible to uphold because the difference between the two states are so steep.

And the split happens right in the middle of your life's greatest tests - when you are at your most powerful but also the most vulnerable, where the world feels like it is destined to unfold before you completely, where nothing feels out of reach, yet at the same time life itself seems to slip away through your fingers as if the hopelessness it makes you feel is structured as some incredibly well-scripted cosmic joke (in many ways, it is).

But that is exactly what the test is. That is the test for mastery, not the illusion of it that is offered and denied to you in the material world within your incarnation.

Like I said, the contrast is simply too great for most.

In one timeline, on one version of your spiritual journey, you shine with the fury of a thousand suns - you are powerful, strong, respected, destined to be in the spotlight but eventually and inevitably corrupted by the desire to enact your own will upon the world - and fail.

It is exactly that moment where you stop where you fail the final test of your mastery. Not of worldly mastery but spiritual mastery that requires of you proof that you can wield your incredible spiritual potential into the afterlife.

On the other hand, in the second timeline, you are a nobody - your worldly potential is never fully realized and produced, you are not celebrated, you are not cherished and loved by the masses, you are never recognized as a master and your potential is overshadowed by the achievements and legacies of others - you must live in total and absolute humbleness and self-denial, keeping that incredible potential at bay.

You may have to endure great loss, grief, trauma, disappointment, etc. but still find the inner wisdom to accept it without breaking spiritually and mentally.

The irony and paradox of it all is that, regardless of whichever path you choose, your role will still be enacted - either through quiet influence or an explosive life and tragic death. It is impossible for you to fail, in the grander scheme of things.

But on a personal level - it is almost impossible not to fail.

The question then was never about whether you'd fulfill your grander destiny for the world, because the forces that sent you to do so will achieve its goal through you regardless - this is why you were perfect for the job in the first place.

The question was about what you would choose for your own fate. How you'd come to know your own self through the journey as the sufferer and then accepter of life.

You are not allowed to change the destiny of the world because the world is simply greater than you. You may simply delay it for a time. Its destiny will be enacted regardless.

But what you are allowed to choose is your own fate - the path you take to get there. You are allowed grace in this department and quite a lot of liberty.

The tragedy of the maven with the inner potential to bend and weave reality to their will is almost always culminated by spiritual corruption. This is expressed in varying degrees in many different people, of course.

But the very few times corruption does not persevere - we get a Christ-like character that raises up the world and fast-forwards it into greater destiny and progress.

text:
This is so good. Worth reading. George Lucas compared Anakin to Faust, making a deal with the devil that ultimately fails.

“Anakin wants to have a family. He wants to be married to Padmé and have children. When he sees in his dreams that Padmé is going to die, he doesn't know how, but it's preordained. 

He's in love with her. He doesn't want her to die. He wants to possess her, to control that. He keeps getting himself deeper and deeper into this pickle. 

He wants a family but at the same time he knows he can't have one. Now the greed has taken over and the fear of losing his wife and baby. The whole point is you can't possess somebody because they are their own person. You can't dominate and make them do everything you want them to do... 

…Right. He's walking into a death trap. And there’s no way out... 

…And also saying that ‘My mentor told me that there was a way that could stop death.'’ Which was a lie. They can't. Anakin got sold a bill of goods because he wanted it so bad that if anybody would sell him anything, he'd believe it... 

It's a scam. Anakin’s made a pact with the Devil: ‘I want the power to save somebody from death. I want to be able to stop them from going to the river Styx, and I need to go to a god for that, but the gods won't do it, so I'm going to go down to Hades and get the dark lord to allow me to have this power that will allow me to save the person I want to hang on to.’ 

Ultimately, it's about power. He traded his soul for power. It's Faust. 

The more power he wants, the more power he gets, the more he loses. The Devil says, ‘You can become more powerful but you must pass this first test. The first test is you must kill your mother. The second test: you have to kill your wife. And the third test: you have to kill your best friend.’ 

In the end you have all this power but you have nobody to share with, except some wizened old man who’s even more evil than you are. 

If you’re going to sell your soul to save somebody you love, that’s, as we say in the film, unnatural. You have to accept the natural course of life. Death is obviously the biggest of them all. Not only death for yourself but death for the things you care about.”

— George Lucas in conversation with Paul Duncan. The Star Wars Archives: 1999–2005 (Published by Taschen)

PGMN Lead Anchor @HirroCj88205 refused to apologize or retract her investigative reports involving former Quezon City 4th District Rep. Marvin Rillo despite facing seven cyberlibel charges filed by the former lawmaker.

In an Oct. 30 statement, Hirro confirmed that she voluntarily appeared before Branch 90 of the Quezon City Regional Trial Court with her three-year-old daughter to post ₱336,000 in cash bail. She was subsequently granted provisional liberty.

The dispute stems from Hirro's investigative episodes questioning government spending, infrastructure projects and Rillo's public statements.

Central to her reporting was the ₱71-million Carlos L. Albert High School gymnasium project. Hirro cited bidding documents covering roofing, flooring, doors and windows, questioning why the site reportedly had only foundations and posts more than a year later.

Rillo's camp maintained that construction covered only the project's first phase, an explanation Hirro challenged based on the bidding documents.

According to Hirro, Rillo filed his complaint in July 2025, following his reelection defeat. The seven charges arose from two videos published across multiple social media platforms.

Hirro said prosecutors recognized her gymnasium reporting as fair comment based on government records. She added that another portion of the complaint concerning public spending was dismissed, alongside complaints against PGMN officers, including Founder and CEO Franco Mabanta.

Following the arrest warrant, Rillo offered to withdraw his complaint if Hirro apologized, warning that additional libel cases could follow if she refused.

“I have never sought his forgiveness, nor do I require it,” Hirro responded.

She emphasized that an arrest warrant does not establish guilt, as prosecutors must still prove the charges beyond reasonable doubt.

“I have no intention of apologizing for doing my job as a journalist. I have no intention of retracting findings that I believe are supported by evidence,” she declared.

Hirro reaffirmed her commitment to investigating public spending and holding elected officials accountable.

Oracle has scrapped a multibillion-dollar chip leasing contract with 🇨🇳 Tencent after bowing to pressure from the Trump administration, in a sign of rising tensions for US cloud providers serving Chinese AI companies.

Oracle signed a 5-year lease with Tencent to provide access to as many as 100,000 advanced AI chips across a host of data centers in southeast Asia.

The contract, worth an estimated $7B, was Tencent’s largest overseas leasing deal. It would have given the group access to chips unavailable for use in China due to curbs from Washington and Beijing.

US officials approached Oracle to raise concerns about the Tencent deal. Tencent also received visits from top officials in Guangdong, where the group is based, who asked the tech giant to support domestic Chinese chips. The deal has since been cancelled.

The incident shows the growing difficulties for leading US and Chinese companies in developing AI, at a time their respective nations seek to become the pre-eminent technological superpower.

A shortage of domestic supply and tightening American export controls have led Chinese tech groups to seek more computing capacity overseas. Such lease deals could also offer access to Nvidia’s cutting-edge processors not available in China.

Chinese tech giants and frontier AI labs are tapping into these resources especially for the training of their models, as domestic chips cannot perform such tasks yet.

While such overseas leasing deals are allowed under existing rules, US companies have faced growing pressure to cut the exposure to Chinese customers. Nvidia has told cloud computing clients that they must now sell at least 51% of their services to non-Chinese companies.

While Tencent is catching up with multibillion leasing deals, ByteDance and Alibaba remain the biggest clients of data centers in southeast Asia.

Oracle is a major supplier to ByteDance in Asia with multiple data centers in Malaysia. The company also hosted US customer data for the Chinese group’s social media platform TikTok before being part of a consortium that late last year acquired the reel-based app’s US operations.

Demand from Chinese AI companies in southeast Asia has intensified amid a tightening in export controls that prevent Nvidia’s advanced chips from entering China via an intermediate location. This has led to increased prices, longer terms and higher upfront payments for these data centre lease agreements.

Tencent’s infrastructure spending has soared in the past year as it continues to catch up in AI capabilities. The Chinese giant’s latest Hunyuan models have shown substantial improvements in performance, closing the gap with top-tier domestic models such as Alibaba’s Qwen.

text:
I don't understand people who call Trump a Republican. He has no principles, and he wasn't a Democrat either when he belonged to the Democratic Party. Trump is a symptom of a political system that has stopped doing its job. He offers simple answers to complex questions, but those answers don't exist. The fact that America has survived him so far doesn't mean the system doesn't need reform. Trump simply turned out to be a cure worse than the disease.

America faces enormous problems abroad. The UN is ineffective, international justice is failing, NATO struggles to fulfill its responsibilities, and wars continue. At home, public education is deteriorating, housing is increasingly unaffordable, racial divisions remain unresolved, the war on drugs has failed, and the Washington swamp is alive and well.

Even the electoral system is outdated. Politics cannot be reduced to two opposing camps. People have different views on economics, individual freedoms, immigration, foreign policy, government, and technology. Someone can support free markets and same-sex marriage, or favor a strong welfare state while opposing immigration. Yet American politics insists on forcing everyone into two competing tribes.

The 2018 Hidden Tribes study identified seven distinct groups within American society and found that roughly two-thirds of Americans belong to an "Exhausted Majority" that rejects political extremes.

High voter turnout is encouraging, but both parties have become experts at mobilizing voters through fear of the other side. They are far less successful at negotiating meaningful reforms. Political competition has become an endless argument about who deserves the blame rather than who can actually solve the problems.

And that is exactly how Trump became possible. He told Americans that everyone had been lying to them, that he was different, and that he would destroy the corrupt system. The less capable that system was of defending itself, the more convincing his promises sounded. Millions were willing to overlook his cruelty, dishonesty, and staggering incompetence because they desperately wanted a quick solution.

But there is no magic pill.

Imagine a patient suffering from a serious chronic illness. Instead of diagnosing the problem, the doctor recommends immediately stopping every treatment and throwing away all medical equipment. Perhaps some treatments were ineffective, the doctors made mistakes, and the hospital desperately needed renovation. But demolishing the hospital is not a cure.

That is Trump's approach to government. And millions of his supporters are prepared to sacrifice democratic institutions for the promise of an instant miracle.

Yet institutions exist precisely because human beings are imperfect. People make mistakes, pursue personal interests, abuse power, and surrender to emotions. A functioning democracy cannot depend on finding a perfect leader. Its institutions must be strong enough to survive mediocre presidents and even disastrous ones.

I hope Trump will not succeed in breaking America. But surviving Trump is not enough. The country needs fundamental reforms, not another political savior promising miracles.

The most dangerous illusion is believing that America must choose between Trump and a return to the old political order. That is a false choice. The old order created the conditions that made Trump possible.

America needs institutions that work, accountable leaders, affordable housing, better education, and a political system that solves problems instead of exploiting them.

Trump is not the solution. He is the warning.

Change. We are waiting for change.

Session LIII
Introduction
Serial murder is one type of homicide which involves the killing of three or more people
for one month and is characterized by a period of cooling off. The cooling-off period is a time
whereby the killers do not commit any murder (Knight, 2006, p. 1192). The people who commit
serial murder are known as serial killers. The crime is not recognized in the United States., as
there is no current legal code on it. In the history of serial killing, the earliest recorded case of
serial killers was in 69 CE in the Roman Empire. The serial killer by the name Locusta was
executed for poisoning individuals from the royal family. In the middle ages, there were serial
killers recorded in European countries (Vronsky, 2018, p. 15). It has likely been occurring in
other parts of the world, though it might not be recorded. Research has attempted to suggest
explanations of the behavior of serial killers and provide an analysis of their personal
development (Ostrosky & Alfredo, 2017, p. 70). There are two types of serial killers, such as
child and adult serial killers, in essence (Harmening, 2014, p. 102). A great number of theories
has been developed to address their actions. Most serial killers have psychological issues, and it
is through killing that they feel satisfied. History has introduced many serial killers, who are
adults, but in recent decades the cases connected with children, who are serial killers, are
becoming frequent. They are dangerous, just like the adults, as they indicate the same
psychological behavior (Knight, 2006, p. 1198).
Types of Serial Killers
Hedonistic Serial Killers
These are serial killers, who receive pleasure from killing, and thus the experience of
murder gives them pleasure. There is a strong link between the violence of the murder and the
sexual gratification. They can have sex with the victim before or after killing the victim (James
& Proulx, 2014, p. 595). They plan their crime well, and they dismember the body of the victim
after the murder. They have an insatiable hunger when they feel that it could be satisfied only by
killing. An example of a serial killer of this category is Jeffrey Dahmer, who was a serial killer in
the period between 1978 and 1991 (Ostrosky & Alfredo, 2017, p. 77).
Power and Control Serial Killers
These serial killers need to exercise their power and control the victim. They first
humiliate the victim, torture, and then kill their victim. They do not respect the law of the land,
and they feel that they are above the law. They also seek sexual gratification. Their main goal is
to gain power and domination, and thus killing makes them feel powerful and in control. Anyone
they feel to be threating to them is killed as they assert dominance (Vronsky, 2018, p. 49).
Visionary Serial Killers
The serial killers in this category are considered psychotic, as their visions and other dark
forces compel them to commit murder. Whoever these voices and visions tell them to kill; these
killers go ahead and kill them. Some of them have undertaken psychiatric tests, which proved
their being mentally unstable. Some of this type of serial killers are possessed by evil forces,
which drive them to kill.  
Mission-Oriented Serial Killers
These are considered as ordinary persons, and they kill a particular group of people. They
may focus on killing people from a specific religion, social class, or race. Their goal is to
eliminate the group or exterminate as many of its members as possible. An example of these
serial killers is Joseph Paul Franklin, who killed young black males, because they had white
girlfriends (Vronsky, 2018, p. 78).
Characteristics of Serial Killers
There are numerous characteristics of serial killers, and these are some of them. First,
serial killers indicate varying levels of psychopathy, which leads to destructive tendencies. They
are mostly categorized in the type of visionary serial killers. They see things and forces which
compel them to kill certain people or group of people. After their action, psychotic serial killers
are gratified and do not show any remorse. In normal circumstances, they are charming and
brilliant. Psychiatrists have identified that these people can be dangerous because people will not
know if they are vulnerable until they become victims of their psychopathic actions. (Ostrosky &
Alfredo, 2017, p. 73). The second characteristic is that when they were young, most serial killers
were abused in the family. The abuse might have been emotional, physical, and sexual. This
abuse causes them to be bitter and sometimes seek revenge by killing people (Knight, 2006, p.
1194).
The other characteristic of serial killers is that they are aroused by the activity, and they
find pleasure in the action. Another aspect is that some of them experience one or all the
Macdonald triad predictors of future violent behavior. The Macdonald triad predictors are a
fascination with fire-setting, involvement in sadistic actions, and bed-wetting (Seltzer, 2013, p.
112). The serial killers were isolated during their childhood and teenage years. This isolation
involved bullying, and the person is seeking to prove that no one can bully him or her since he or
she has grown up. Some of the serial killers’ targets are people who bullied them or showed
particular behavior associated with bullying (Carlisle, 2017, p. 17). Some other characteristics
are that the serial killers might have been involved in petty crimes, and they had trouble staying
